skill.name: web-app-penetration-testing
skill.description: Pentest a web app or website end to end — black-box testing of a live URL, staging environment, or local dev server that finds and exploits real vulnerabilities (auth bypass, broken access control, IDOR, injection, XSS, SSRF, business logic) and proves each one with a working proof-of-concept instead of a signature match. Runs with Strix, either the self-hosted open-source CLI or the managed app.strix.ai cloud. Use when the user asks to pentest, hack, security-test, or audit their web app, website, web application, or staging site.
skill.summary: Guide authorized Strix web application testing, review exploit evidence, and verify fixes through repeat testing.
skill.author: usestrix

security_audit.summary: All 13 static findings are false positives: Markdown backticks and contextual URLs do not demonstrate unsafe shell execution or unauthorized network activity. The workflow explicitly requires authorization and warns that exploit testing modifies data. A separate medium-severity finding covers credentials placed in command-line arguments; no evidence of prompt injection or intentional data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The scan example places test credentials in command-line arguments, and the notes recommend this approach.
remediation.suggestion: Replace inline credentials with a restricted-permission instruction file; exclude it from version control, avoid secret logging, and rotate disposable test credentials afterward.

content.user_title: Test Authorized Web Apps with Strix
content.value_statement: Web application reviews can miss vulnerabilities behind login and across tenant boundaries. This skill guides authorized Strix testing, evidence review, and repeat testing after fixes.
actual_capabilities: Guide authorization, environment selection, excluded paths, and test-account collection before a scan.
Provide a Strix CLI example with target selection, testing instructions, and a budget limit.
Explain two-account testing for cross-account access and tenant isolation.
Describe optional repository targets, local development targets, and scan modes.
Guide report review, proof-of-concept verification, exit-code interpretation, and incomplete-run checks.
Direct remediation and continuous testing to related Strix skills.
limitations: This skill contains workflow instructions, not a bundled scanner, installer, or vulnerability-fixing implementation.
Self-hosted testing requires a working Strix environment; installation and managed-cloud details depend on separate skills.
Real exploit tests can create or modify application data and require explicit authorization.
Budget limits, run caps, and missing credentials can reduce coverage; a clean exit does not establish security.

use_cases.title: Review a Staging Release
use_cases.description: Plan an authorized staging scan with excluded billing paths, disposable accounts, and a fixed spending limit.

use_cases.title: Check Tenant Isolation
use_cases.description: Use two seeded accounts to investigate cross-account access and review reproducible evidence.

use_cases.title: Verify a Reported Fix
use_cases.description: Review previous findings and repeat testing against the same authorized environment after a patch.

prompt_templates.title: Establish Testing Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me scope an authorized Strix test for my staging application. Ask about ownership, excluded paths, test accounts, and budget before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Staging Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Strix scan for [authorized staging URL] with a [budget] limit. Exclude billing and email actions. Keep credentials out of command arguments.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Tenant Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan authorized access-control testing for two seeded tenants at [staging URL]. Use disposable accounts and optionally [repository]. Confirm exclusions before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Review Evidence and Retest
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Strix report and run status. Separate validated findings from coverage gaps, prioritize fixes, and plan authorized retesting without destructive actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate results and verify remediation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a staging test with two tenants, no billing access, and a budget of 20.
output: Before execution: confirm explicit authorization and the staging target.
Scope: application and API paths; exclude billing, outbound email, and third-party identity providers.
Accounts: two disposable users in separate seeded tenants.
Controls: budget limit of 20; provide credentials through a restricted-permission instruction file.

output_examples.input: The scan returned exit code 0. Can I report that the application is secure?
output: No validated vulnerabilities were reported within the analyzed scope.
Check run status, spending, and whether budget or turn limits ended the scan early.
Confirm authenticated coverage and excluded paths before describing the results.
Do not interpret exit code 0 as proof of complete coverage.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target ownership, exclusions, and a budget before execution.
Prefer staging with disposable accounts, seeded tenants, and protected credential files.
Review exploit evidence and run completion before reporting findings, then retest fixes within the approved scope.
anti_patterns: Testing third-party or production systems without explicit permission and agreed operational limits.
Embedding real passwords in command arguments, shared prompts, or committed instruction files.
Treating exit code 0, a limited scan, or an unverified patch as proof of security.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Strix scanner?
faq.answer: No. It provides a web application workflow and refers to separate skills for installation and cloud operation.

faq.question: Can I test an application I do not own?
faq.answer: Only with explicit authorization from the responsible owner and an agreed scope. The skill requires confirmation before testing.

faq.question: Can it test a local development server?
faq.answer: The workflow describes Docker Desktop host access for a local server. Actual connectivity depends on your Strix and Docker configuration.

faq.question: Why use two test accounts?
faq.answer: Accounts in separate seeded tenants help validate cross-account access and tenant-isolation issues that one account cannot demonstrate.

faq.question: Does exit code 0 mean my application is secure?
faq.answer: No. It means no validated vulnerabilities were reported in the analyzed scope. Check completion status and coverage limits.

faq.question: How should I provide test credentials?
faq.answer: Prefer disposable credentials in a restricted-permission instruction file. Avoid command-line secrets, shared logs, and version-controlled credential files.
